intro.title: Overflow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with a fixed-size container to explore how CSS handles content that is too large for its box. You will learn the core concept of the CSS overflow property, which controls what happens when content overflows an element's boundaries. The main technologies involved are CSS properties like overflow, overflow-x, and overflow-y, applied to a div element. You will practice setting values such as visible, hidden, scroll, and auto to manage overflowing text and images. By the end, you'll understand how to prevent layout issues and create scrollable areas when needed.
intro.usecase: The CSS overflow property is essential for managing content that exceeds its container's boundaries in real-world interfaces. Developers use it in dashboards to create scrollable data tables, in e-commerce sites for product filter panels with many options, and in messaging apps for chat histories that need vertical scrolling. Social media platforms implement overflow:hidden for cropping profile pictures into circles, while documentation sites use overflow:auto for code blocks with horizontal scrolling. These practical applications ensure clean, controlled layouts regardless of content size.
